summary: We screened 26 Death Valley windows against five overlapping squares on Jezero’s mapped western delta using open elevation products. R03C04, in the C04 strip, ranked in the top three for slope in 81 of 90 sensitivity cases. Jezero retained substantially more steep terrain than the leading Death Valley windows. The result gives us a starting point for comparing coarse rover route alternatives on maps and planning finer validation.
details:
Problem and approach

For the NASA Space Apps terrain analog challenge, we focused on which Death Valley terrain to inspect for a Jezero route-planning exercise. We used a 5 × 5 grid of 2.16 km Earth squares and a Trail Canyon reference. We compared slope, local relief and detrended roughness using separate empirical Wasserstein distances (W1). We averaged 49 bilinear elevation samples per output cell and used central differences for slope. The 90 m tests crossed five overlapping Jezero windows with nine Earth shifts and two Earth DEMs. Each shift translates the whole Earth grid by the same offset. The 90 cases share footprints and data.

Findings

  • Inspect R03C04 first. It ranked in the top three 81/90 times (48 firsts). R05C04 did so 63/90 times (13 firsts). In the original Jezero window, their slope W1 values are 1.424° and 1.308° in NASADEM, and 1.441° and 1.479° in Copernicus. The change in DEM reverses their order for this case.
  • The steep tail is a poor match. The four Jezero offsets differ from the original window by 0.362°–0.961° in slope W1. At nominal centers R03C04 is 1.424°–1.441° away, and its P90 slope is about 4.4° compared with 8.07° in the original Jezero window. Jezero has 76/484 cells above 6°. R03C04, R05C04 and Trail have zero in both Earth products.
  • Roughness remains unresolved. The DEM change moves the two highlighted roughness distances more than the nominal Trail–R05C04 gap. An exploratory circular mask around the Jezero low leaves 165 of 256 complete relief neighborhoods at 270 m. We recomputed all three Mars features and reranked all 26 Earth windows with each DEM. The low’s geological identity remains open.

Use and limits

Start with R03C04 and adjacent C04 windows for desktop rehearsal of comparing coarse rover route options. Trail Canyon and R05C03 share about 43% of the Trail footprint, so the windows provide spatial comparisons with partial redundancy. The coarse California map puts Trail’s sampled centers at 99.65% older alluvium (Qoa) and 0.35% younger alluvium (Q). R05C04 is 100% Q. These classes do not establish a matching depositional process. Higher resolution imagery, surface geology, obstacles, traction and access need separate checks before field rehearsal. The elevation data cannot reproduce Martian gravity or atmosphere.

Reproduction and sources

The project package includes documented inputs and checksums, pinned NumPy and Pillow versions, expected-output CSVs, scripts, rankings, figures, and a seven-slide PDF. It links the source rasters separately. The NASADEM source-index layer (NUM) exists in the full product. The elevation mirror used here omits it, so actual interpolation flags remain unchecked.

OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assisted with research, analysis code, and slide and text drafting. Claude assisted with critical review. Measurements and maps were computed using the source data. The README gives source terms and the Copernicus adapted-data notice.
